messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Pager: inference-az1a-high-latency triggered at 2026-03-15T02:04:16Z
charlie-sre: seeing sudden spikes in p99 token latency for az1a, started ~02:02 UTC
maya-oncall: i'm on it, pulling graphs and logs now
maya-oncall: metric snapshot: inference.latency.p99{region=az1a}=1.8s (+3x baseline)
sam-runtime: noticing 502/504 retries at the proxy layer, queue depth up on inference-proxy pods
sam-runtime: logs show repeated "connection reset by peer" and kvcache miss retries across multiple replicas
lee-infra: cloudwatch shows ENI attach failures and ENI-queue-saturation warnings on a subset of g5 hosts in az1a
lee-infra: AWS console note: transient control-plane API throttling in az1a (no full region outage) — correlates with our errors
charlie-sre: incident created INC-2026-1273 (Sev2) — assigning initial responders
maya-oncall: initial mitigation: enable cross-az failover for inference routes and shift low-priority Dedicated traffic to eu1 to reduce pressure on az1a
maya-oncall: running runbook step: reroute
```bash
redwood ctl route update --selector=prod-inference-az1a --mode=failover --target-region=eu1
```
maya-oncall: initiated reroute at 02:12 UTC
sam-runtime: spinning up replacement capacity in az1b + eu1 (on-demand to avoid spot ENI attach races)
sam-runtime: note: model kvcache warmups mean short-term token latency spikes expected while new nodes warm
alice-cs: CS: prepping customer comms, flagging Dedicated customers in NA that might see higher latency/503s
support-bot: Status page updated: "Partial degradation in az1a affecting inference latency" — https://status.redwood.com/INC-2026-1273
charlie-sre: after reroute, RPS to az1a dropped but sticky sessions still directing some traffic back, causing retries
sam-runtime: forcing sticky-session TTL reset on inference-proxy to break old connections
maya-oncall: Command to restart proxies:
```bash
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/inference-proxy
```
maya-oncall: restart kicked at 02:18 UTC, watching for reconnections
lee-infra: infra team starting node drain on 3 hosts showing ENI flapping, requesting reattach window from AWS (rate-limited)
lee-infra: converting some spot replacements to on-demand to reduce attach throttles
charlie-sre: any hard customer errors reported? quantify impact
alice-cs: CS report: 7 high-sev customer tickets in last 20m, all reporting timeouts or partial failures for inference calls
charlie-sre: telemetry: backend 5xx increased ~12% in last 15m, top impacted models redwood-base-2 and embed-xlarge
maya-oncall: implement temporary model-fallback: route redwood-base-2 -> redwood-base-2-quant for az1a requests to reduce per-token CPU pressure
sam-runtime: deploying routing policy for model fallback at 02:23 UTC
maya-oncall: handoff: charlie, do you want to stay primary?
charlie-sre: handing primary to maya, I need a short break. I'll remain on-call for escalations. handoff at 02:30 UTC
maya-oncall: taking lead. summary: (1) cross-az failover in progress, (2) draining 3 noisy hosts, (3) model fallback enabled, (4) CS notified and status page updated
maya-oncall: next decision point in 15m: if p99 not <1s, escalate to full instance replacement and request increased AZ capacity
lee-infra: running emergency instance replacement for the 3 impacted hosts, converting to on-demand, likely available in ~8-12m
support-bot: CS message sent to affected customers: "We're investigating elevated latency in NA (az1a). We've routed traffic to healthy AZs and expect improvements within 15-30 minutes."
alice-cs: adding customers to private updates: Acct-123, Acct-456, Acct-789
sam-runtime: p99 trending down to ~900ms after failover + proxy restart, still seeing intermittent spikes tied to kvcache repopulation
maya-oncall: noted. keep model-fallback on for at least 1h post-stabilization
charlie-sre: checking downstream systems: no bulk queueing in ingestion pipelines, backpressure limited to proxy layer
maya-oncall: request to infra: confirm ENI attach errors cleared for >30m before unfreezing routing back to az1a
lee-infra: ENI attach error rate dropping, AWS confirmed control-plane throttles subsiding; we'll wait 30m from last flap before full shiftback
alice-cs: CS will follow up in 1h with affected accounts, escalate immediate outstanding tickets now
charlie-sre: creating initial incident timeline for postmortem, capturing mitigation steps and timestamps
maya-oncall: postmortem owners: lee-infra + sam-runtime — include AWS ENI attach metrics, pod-level connection resets, and model fallback impact analysis
incident-bot: INC-2026-1273 status changed to "stabilized" at 02:45 UTC — responders: charlie-sre, maya-oncall, sam-runtime, lee-infra, alice-cs
maya-oncall: handing monitoring to morning shift (olivia-sre) for watch and postmortem follow-up
maya-oncall: leaving channel but available on pager; checklist: reroute maintained, model-fallback set, CS follow-up scheduled
charlie-sre: final: monitoring shows stable p99 < 1s for 25m, incident to be closed after 1h of stability and CS confirmation
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1273 closed at 03:04 UTC
